function.name: read
function.description: Read a text file. Paths are relative to the project directory. Output is cut at 2000 lines or 50 KB (lines over 2000 chars are cut); a note at the end tells you the offset to continue from.

path.description: File path, relative to the project directory

function.name: write
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely, with the given content. Parent directories are created automatically. For changing part of an existing file use edit instead.

path.description: File path, relative to the project directory

content.description: The full new content of the file

function.name: edit
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. old_string must match the file exactly (including whitespace and indentation) and occur exactly once; add surrounding lines to make it unique, or set replace_all. Read the file first.

path.description: File path, relative to the project directory

new_string.description: Text to put in its place

function.name: bash
function.description: Run a bash command in the project directory and return stdout and stderr combined. stdin is empty (no interactive input). Timeout defaults to 120 s (max 600). Only the last 2000 lines / 50 KB of output are kept. A non-zero exit or timeout is reported as an error with the output. Background processes are killed when the command finishes.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents for a regular expression (ripgrep syntax; skips .gitignore'd and binary files). Returns matching lines as path:line:text. Stops at 200 lines by default.

pattern.description: Regular expression (or plain text with literal=true)

path.description: File or directory to search (default: whole project)

glob.description: Only search files whose name matches this glob, e.g. *.py

literal.description: Treat pattern as plain text (default false)

context.description: Lines of context around each match (0-20, default 0)

function.name: find
function.description: Find files and directories by glob. A pattern without / matches names at any depth (e.g. *.py); a pattern with / matches the path from the search directory (e.g. src/**/*.ts). Directories end with /. Skips .git.

function.name: ls
function.description: List a directory, sorted by name. Directories end with /. Includes hidden entries.
